1	# Changelog — QA Agent Pipeline
2	
3	All notable changes to this pipeline (not to any project it's used on) are logged here.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	### Removed
7	- OpenCode support. The pipeline now generates and targets Claude Code only — `.opencode/` is
8	  gone, `scripts/generate_agents.py` no longer writes OpenCode agent/command files, and
9	  OpenCode references have been removed from the docs.
10	
11	### Added
12	- **`dashboard/`** — an optional local web UI (FastAPI + vanilla JS, `python3
13	  dashboard/server.py`) with a button per agent, a full-pipeline runner, a live streamed log, and
14	  a browser for `output/` artifacts (markdown rendered, CSV as a table). Every action is a thin
15	  wrapper around the same `claude` CLI invocations documented in the README — no new agent
16	  behavior. Includes a UI-side Approve step surfaced after `test-planner` runs, mirroring the
17	  existing human review gate before `test-case-writer` is unlocked.
18	- **QA-friendly, real-user-behavior language required throughout.** `code-scanner`'s discovered
19	  business rules, `requirements-analyzer`'s mismatch findings, and every `test-case-writer`
20	  step/expected-result must be phrased in terms of what a real user does and sees — never code
21	  identifiers or internal implementation details — so QA engineers can act on them without
22	  reading the underlying code.
23	- `code-scanner` now also extracts business rules, validation logic, feature flags, and
24	  integration points from the changed code it already reviews (`## Business Rules & Behavior
25	  Discovered` in `code-scan.md`), each with a `file:line` citation, in plain user-facing language.
26	- `requirements-analyzer` now cross-references requirements against `code-scan.md`'s discovered
27	  business rules (if that stage has run this cycle), surfacing an `## Implementation vs.
28	  Documentation Mismatches` section: documented-but-unconfirmed, implemented-but-undocumented,
29	  and directly conflicting behavior.
30	- **Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM).** `requirements-analyzer` seeds `output/rtm.md` +
31	  `rtm.csv` (Requirement ID → Source Ref → Implementation Ref → Test Case ID(s) → Test Status →
32	  Defect ID(s)) whenever a requirements document exists this cycle; `test-case-writer` and
33	  `bug-reporter` fill in the remaining columns as the cycle progresses. No RTM is produced when
34	  there's no requirements document, same as `requirements.md` itself.
35	- Test cases now carry explicit **Origin** (Requirement-based / Implementation-based),
36	  **Category** (Functional / Regression / Boundary / Negative / Security / Accessibility), and
37	  **Automation Candidate** (Yes/No + reason) fields, replacing the old free-text
38	  Positive/Negative/Edge type — grouped so a reviewer can scan by origin, by risk category, or by
39	  automation candidates. `test-cases.csv` gains matching columns.
40	- **Structured clarification questions.** `test-plan.md`'s Open Questions section is now a table
41	  (Question / Context / Source / Related Scope Area), aggregated by `test-planner` from its own
42	  uncertain impact areas, `requirements.md` mismatches, and vague code behavior noted in
43	  `code-scan.md` — every question cites a concrete source. These are for the user to review with
44	  Product/Dev; the pipeline never answers them itself.
45	- `test-planner`'s risk classification now explicitly names its four inputs: code complexity,
46	  business impact, data sensitivity, and module dependencies (wording clarification; the
47	  High/Medium/Low rating and review gate were already in place).
48	- `config/pipeline.config.yaml` — configurable output directory/file names, read by every
49	  agent instead of hardcoding `output/`.
50	- `qa-pipeline` orchestrator command (`.claude/commands/`, `.opencode/commands/`) that chains
51	  named stages in sequence, enforcing the test-plan review gate automatically.
52	- `scripts/generate_agents.py` now also generates commands (`config/commands.yaml` +
53	  `prompts/commands/`), same pattern as agents.
54	- **Run-versioned output.** `config/pipeline.config.yaml` gains `runs_subdir` and `run_id`;
55	  every stage's output now lives under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/`, resolved from
56	  config, a user-stated run/release identifier, or today's date — except `context.md`, which
57	  stays unversioned at `<output_dir>/context.md`. Every agent states which `run_id` it used, and
58	  which run folder it read from when inferring one. All stages in a single `/qa-pipeline`
59	  invocation share one resolved `run_id`.
60	- **`requirements-analyzer`** (optional agent) — extracts CR/requirement items from an SRS/CR
61	  document and cross-references them against `changes.md`, producing `requirements.md`. Says so
62	  plainly and stops if no requirements document is available; never fabricates requirements from
63	  the codebase.
64	- **`code-scanner`** — reviews only the changed code recorded in a run's `changes.md` for logic
65	  bugs, weak error handling, security concerns, convention violations, and leftover debug code,
66	  producing `code-scan.md`. Every finding is Blocker/Should-Fix/Note with a file:line reference.
67	  Advisory only: feeds `test-planner`'s risk rating, never blocks the pipeline.
68	- `test-planner` now optionally reads `requirements.md` (CR traceability) and `code-scan.md`
69	  (reweights risk of in-scope areas by Blocker/Should-Fix findings), and adds a defect-prone
70	  zone heuristic (git churn + historical bug frequency from past runs' `bugs/`) that only
71	  reweights risk on already-in-scope areas and populates an advisory "Known Fragile Areas - Not
72	  In Scope This Release" section — never expands test scope to untouched code. Guardrail: signal
73	  under ~5 historical bugs or a very short churn window is labeled inconclusive, not reweighted.
74	- `test-planner` and `test-case-writer` now always write a CSV (`test-plan.csv`,
75	  `test-cases.csv`) alongside their markdown, every run, for manual import into Google Sheets
76	  (File > Import > Append) — no agent touches Google Sheets or any external tool directly.
77	
78	## [0.1.0] - Initial release
79	### Added
80	- 8 agents covering the full manual QA cycle: context-analyzer, changelog-analyzer,
81	  test-planner, test-case-writer, log-analyzer, rca-analyst, bug-reporter,
82	  release-notes-writer.
83	- Single-source-of-truth prompt files under `prompts/`, generated into both Claude Code
84	  (`.claude/agents/`) and OpenCode (`.opencode/agent/`) formats via
85	  `scripts/generate_agents.py`.
86	- Output templates for every agent under `templates/`.
87	- Read-only-on-source-code tool permissions for every agent.

# Changelog — QA Agent Pipeline

All notable changes to this pipeline (not to any project it's used on) are logged here.

## [Unreleased]
### Removed
- OpenCode support. The pipeline now generates and targets Claude Code only — `.opencode/` is
  gone, `scripts/generate_agents.py` no longer writes OpenCode agent/command files, and
  OpenCode references have been removed from the docs.

### Added
- **`dashboard/`** — an optional local web UI (FastAPI + vanilla JS, `python3
  dashboard/server.py`) with a button per agent, a full-pipeline runner, a live streamed log, and
  a browser for `output/` artifacts (markdown rendered, CSV as a table). Every action is a thin
  wrapper around the same `claude` CLI invocations documented in the README — no new agent
  behavior. Includes a UI-side Approve step surfaced after `test-planner` runs, mirroring the
  existing human review gate before `test-case-writer` is unlocked.
- **QA-friendly, real-user-behavior language required throughout.** `code-scanner`'s discovered
  business rules, `requirements-analyzer`'s mismatch findings, and every `test-case-writer`
  step/expected-result must be phrased in terms of what a real user does and sees — never code
  identifiers or internal implementation details — so QA engineers can act on them without
  reading the underlying code.
- `code-scanner` now also extracts business rules, validation logic, feature flags, and
  integration points from the changed code it already reviews (`## Business Rules & Behavior
  Discovered` in `code-scan.md`), each with a `file:line` citation, in plain user-facing language.
- `requirements-analyzer` now cross-references requirements against `code-scan.md`'s discovered
  business rules (if that stage has run this cycle), surfacing an `## Implementation vs.
  Documentation Mismatches` section: documented-but-unconfirmed, implemented-but-undocumented,
  and directly conflicting behavior.
- **Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM).** `requirements-analyzer` seeds `output/rtm.md` +
  `rtm.csv` (Requirement ID → Source Ref → Implementation Ref → Test Case ID(s) → Test Status →
  Defect ID(s)) whenever a requirements document exists this cycle; `test-case-writer` and
  `bug-reporter` fill in the remaining columns as the cycle progresses. No RTM is produced when
  there's no requirements document, same as `requirements.md` itself.
- Test cases now carry explicit **Origin** (Requirement-based / Implementation-based),
  **Category** (Functional / Regression / Boundary / Negative / Security / Accessibility), and
  **Automation Candidate** (Yes/No + reason) fields, replacing the old free-text
  Positive/Negative/Edge type — grouped so a reviewer can scan by origin, by risk category, or by
  automation candidates. `test-cases.csv` gains matching columns.
- **Structured clarification questions.** `test-plan.md`'s Open Questions section is now a table
  (Question / Context / Source / Related Scope Area), aggregated by `test-planner` from its own
  uncertain impact areas, `requirements.md` mismatches, and vague code behavior noted in
  `code-scan.md` — every question cites a concrete source. These are for the user to review with
  Product/Dev; the pipeline never answers them itself.
- `test-planner`'s risk classification now explicitly names its four inputs: code complexity,
  business impact, data sensitivity, and module dependencies (wording clarification; the
  High/Medium/Low rating and review gate were already in place).
- `config/pipeline.config.yaml` — configurable output directory/file names, read by every
  agent instead of hardcoding `output/`.
- `qa-pipeline` orchestrator command (`.claude/commands/`, `.opencode/commands/`) that chains
  named stages in sequence, enforcing the test-plan review gate automatically.
- `scripts/generate_agents.py` now also generates commands (`config/commands.yaml` +
  `prompts/commands/`), same pattern as agents.
- **Run-versioned output.** `config/pipeline.config.yaml` gains `runs_subdir` and `run_id`;
  every stage's output now lives under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/`, resolved from
  config, a user-stated run/release identifier, or today's date — except `context.md`, which
  stays unversioned at `<output_dir>/context.md`. Every agent states which `run_id` it used, and
  which run folder it read from when inferring one. All stages in a single `/qa-pipeline`
  invocation share one resolved `run_id`.
- **`requirements-analyzer`** (optional agent) — extracts CR/requirement items from an SRS/CR
  document and cross-references them against `changes.md`, producing `requirements.md`. Says so
  plainly and stops if no requirements document is available; never fabricates requirements from
  the codebase.
- **`code-scanner`** — reviews only the changed code recorded in a run's `changes.md` for logic
  bugs, weak error handling, security concerns, convention violations, and leftover debug code,
  producing `code-scan.md`. Every finding is Blocker/Should-Fix/Note with a file:line reference.
  Advisory only: feeds `test-planner`'s risk rating, never blocks the pipeline.
- `test-planner` now optionally reads `requirements.md` (CR traceability) and `code-scan.md`
  (reweights risk of in-scope areas by Blocker/Should-Fix findings), and adds a defect-prone
  zone heuristic (git churn + historical bug frequency from past runs' `bugs/`) that only
  reweights risk on already-in-scope areas and populates an advisory "Known Fragile Areas - Not
  In Scope This Release" section — never expands test scope to untouched code. Guardrail: signal
  under ~5 historical bugs or a very short churn window is labeled inconclusive, not reweighted.
- `test-planner` and `test-case-writer` now always write a CSV (`test-plan.csv`,
  `test-cases.csv`) alongside their markdown, every run, for manual import into Google Sheets
  (File > Import > Append) — no agent touches Google Sheets or any external tool directly.

## [0.1.0] - Initial release
### Added
- 8 agents covering the full manual QA cycle: context-analyzer, changelog-analyzer,
  test-planner, test-case-writer, log-analyzer, rca-analyst, bug-reporter,
  release-notes-writer.
- Single-source-of-truth prompt files under `prompts/`, generated into both Claude Code
  (`.claude/agents/`) and OpenCode (`.opencode/agent/`) formats via
  `scripts/generate_agents.py`.

- Read-only-on-source-code tool permissions for every agent.

14	
15	## Overview
16	`rsc-service` ("Roaming Status Check API for M1", version `2.0.5`, `pom.xml`) is a telecom backend built for M1 Singapore. It checks whether a given MSISDN (mobile subscriber number) is currently roaming by querying the operator's HLR/VLR data through an SPML provisioning-gateway connector, caches results, logs transactions/events, and exposes reporting on those transactions through a separate web UI. It is a Maven multi-module project with three deployable modules: a reactive API service, a log/report data loader, and a Thymeleaf/Keycloak-secured report viewer (`pom.xml` `<modules>`).
17	
18	## Tech Stack
19	- **Language/runtime**: Kotlin 1.9.25 (main API + data loader), Java 21 (report viewer), JDK 21 target (`pom.xml` `java.version`).
20	- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.5.6 (parent POM), Spring WebFlux + Kotlin coroutines (`rsc-service-api`), Spring MVC + Thymeleaf (`rsc-report-viewer`), Spring Data JDBC/JPA.
21	- **Build**: Maven, multi-module reactor (`rsc-service-parent`).
22	- **Key libraries**: `kotlinx-coroutines-reactor`, `resilience4j` (rate limiter, time limiter) for SPML call protection, `caffeine` (in-memory L1 cache), `mariadb-java-client`, `micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave` + `zipkin-reporter-brave` for distributed tracing, `hms-common-util` / `snmp-log-utils` (internal hSenid libraries for SNMP alarms), `spml-gw` (internal SPML connector library used to talk to the telecom provisioning gateway), Gson, `super-csv` (report export, confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`), `mockk` / `mockito-kotlin` / `spring-boot-starter-test` / `reactor-test` for testing.
23	- **Data store**: MariaDB 11.4 (two logical DBs: `rsc_config_db` for users/config, `rsc_reporting_db`/`rsc-reporting` for transaction & event logs) — confirmed via `application.yml` datasource URLs and `data/config_db*`, `data/reporting_db*` Liquibase changelogs.
24	- **Auth**: `rsc-service-api` uses HTTP Basic-style `Authorization` header (base64 `user:password`) validated against a DB-backed user table (`VisitorAuthenticator.kt`). `rsc-report-viewer` uses OAuth2/OIDC login against Keycloak (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`, `issuer-uri: https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` — confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/resources/application.yml`).
25	- **Infra**: Docker Compose files for local dev DB/infra and Liquibase migrations (`docker/docker-compose-*.yml`, `liquibase.sh`), HAProxy 2.6.0 mentioned as the fronting LB (Readme.md software versions list), RedHat 9.4 target OS.
26	
27	## Architecture
28	Monolith-ish multi-module system, not a single deployable — three independently built/deployed Spring Boot apps sharing the same MariaDB schemas and internal libraries:
29	
30	```
31	Roaming client (e.g. VPE/other operator)
32	      │ HTTPS + Basic Auth  (GET /vpe/api/visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn})
33	      ▼
34	rsc-service-api (WebFlux, functional routers)
35	      │
36	      ├─ auth: VisitorAuthenticator ──► rsc_config_db (users/roles)
37	      ├─ workflow: WorkflowChain (chain-of-responsibility validators)
38	      │     NumberLengthValidator → NumberRangeValidator → CheckInCache →
39	      │     SpmlExistsValidator → SingleMsisdnRoamingValidator → MultiSimStatusValidator
40	      ├─ cache: DistributedMsisdnCacheManager — L1 Caffeine (per-instance) + L2 MariaDB
41	      │     (shared/distributed), background sync (30s) + cleanup (2min) schedulers
42	      ├─ connectors: SpmlConnectorAdapter → spml-gw library → SPML/XML provisioning
43	      │     gateway (HLR/VLR search + multi-SIM member check), rate-limited via resilience4j
44	      ├─ logs: TransLogger / EventLogger → transaction & event log tables/files
45	      └─ snmp: CommonSNMPManager → SNMP traps for DB errors, high TPS, timeouts, start/stop
46	
47	rsc-data-loader (Kotlin, scheduled batch/log processor)
48	      reads trans/event log files → parses via ColumnSpec/Transformers →
49	      writes to rsc_reporting_db (trans_log, tps_log, trx_events_log tables) →
50	      ReportGeneratorService produces summary/detail report tables
51	
52	rsc-report-viewer (Spring MVC + Thymeleaf, Keycloak OAuth2 login)
53	      ReportingController/ReportingService → DetailTransactionRepository (JPA/JDBC)
54	      → reads rsc_reporting_db → renders/downloads CSV reports (super-csv)
55	```
56	
57	## Modules / Components
58	- **rsc-service-api** — Reactive API that answers roaming-status lookups for MSISDNs against the telecom HLR/VLR via SPML, with caching, validation chain, auth, and alarms. Path: `rsc-service-api/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/`
59	  - `api/` — WebFlux functional route definitions (`RouteConfiguration.kt`) for `visitorInfo`, user management (`/user/add`, `/user/update-password`, `/user/change-status`), and cache admin (`/clear-cache`, `/clear-all-cache`).
60	  - `workflow/` — `WorkflowChain`/`WorkFlowStep` chain-of-responsibility pattern driving the roaming-check pipeline and building the response/cache entry.
61	  - `validator/` — individual chain steps: MSISDN length/range checks, SPML existence check, single-MSISDN roaming determination, multi-SIM status check, cache short-circuit (`CheckInCache`).
62	  - `connectors/` — `SpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps the internal `spml-gw` library to send XML SPML requests (`search_request.xml`, `multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`) and parse HLR/VLR/call-barring (odboc) XPath responses.
63	  - `cache/` — `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager` (hybrid L1 Caffeine + L2 MariaDB cache), `CacheRepository`, sync/cleanup schedulers.
64	  - `auth/` — Basic-auth style `VisitorAuthenticator`, DB-backed user repo/entity, `PasswordService`, `UserRoles` (ADMIN/USER).
65	  - `logs/` — `TransLogger`/`EventLogger`/TPS logger writing transaction, event, and TPS logs consumed later by `rsc-data-loader`.
66	  - `snmp/`, `alarms/` — SNMP trap alarms for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, app start/stop.
67	  - `error/` — typed exceptions (`ApiErrorException`, `InternalErrorException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `DefaultErrorException`) mapped to HTTP statuses.
68	- **rsc-data-loader** — Batch/scheduled Kotlin service that parses trans/event/TPS log files and loads them into the reporting DB, then generates summary reports. Path: `rsc-data-loader/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/dataloader/`
69	  - `logspecs/` — column specs and field `Transformer`s (`NullColumnTransformer`, `BooleanFieldTransformer`, `FieldWithColumnNameTransformer`) describing log file layouts.
70	  - `service/lineProcessor/`, `service/loadInFileProcessor/` — log line/file ingestion pipeline (`TransLogProcessor`, `LoadInFileProcessor`).
71	  - `service/reportGenerator/` — `ReportGeneratorService`/`ReportGeneratorRepository` builds summary/detail report tables.
72	  - `service/lock/` — `DistributedTemplateLockManager` (DB-based distributed locking, likely to keep multi-instance loaders from double-processing).
73	  - `snmp/` — SNMP alarm config mirroring the API module.
74	- **rsc-report-viewer** — Spring MVC web app (Java) with Keycloak SSO login for viewing/exporting roaming transaction reports. Path: `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/java/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/viewer/`
75	  - `controller/` — `LoginController`, `ReportingController`.
76	  - `service/`, `service/impl/` — `ReportingService`/`ReportingServiceImpl`.
77	  - `repository/` — `DetailTransactionRepository`, `UserRepository` (JPA).
78	  - `configuration/` — `SecurityConfiguration`, `AuthoritiesConverter`, `CustomAuthenticationEvents` (Keycloak/OAuth2 role mapping).
79	  - `validator/` — `DetailTransactionReportValidator`, `DateFormatValidator` for report query params.
80	  - `health/` — `DbHealthChecker`.
81	  - `keycloak/theme/` — custom Keycloak login theme.
82	- **data/** — Liquibase changelogs for the four MariaDB schemas: `config_db`, `config_db_test`, `reporting_db`, `reporting_db_test`, plus `initial-data/` scripts (user seeding, `trx_events_log`/`trans_log`/`tps_log` partitioning). Path: `data/`
83	- **simulators/rsc-service-simulator/** — WireMock-based standalone simulator (jar + `mappings/`) used to fake SPML/downstream responses for testing (roaming true/false, unauthorized, bad-request, not-acceptable, internal-error scenarios). Path: `simulators/rsc-service-simulator/`
84	- **docs/** — HLD PlantUML/PNG diagrams (system context, API/report-viewer/data-loader component diagrams, deployment, DB designs) under `docs/hld/`, SRS/SOW/flow requirement docs under `docs/req/`, and real SPML XML/WSDL/XSD samples under `docs/spml_samples/`. Path: `docs/`
85	- **Documents/** — Untracked reference material (client-supplied SRS PDFs across versions `v0.0.2`–`v1.1.0`, SDP PDFs, SOW xlsx, flow/sequence diagrams, VPE OpenAPI spec, XSD/WSDL zips). Not code, useful background for requirements analysis. Path: `Documents/`
86	- **QA agent pipeline scaffold** (`config/`, `prompts/`, `templates/`, `output/`, `dashboard/`, `scripts/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`, root `README.md`) — this is tooling for the QA pipeline itself (this analysis run), not part of the deployed rsc-service product; confirmed untracked in `git status` in the target repo. Not a runtime component of the product under test.
87	
88	## Integration Points
89	- **SPML (XML over HTTP, via internal `spml-gw` connector library)** — outbound integration to the telecom Provisioning Gateway for HLR/VLR search (`search_request.xml`) and multi-SIM member check (`multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`); WSDL/XSD in `rsc-service-api/src/main/resources/spml/wsdl/` and `docs/spml_samples/`. Rate-limited to 50 req/s via `resilience4j` (`application.yml` `resilience4j.ratelimiter.instances.spml-requests`).
90	- **REST (Basic Auth) inbound API** — `rsc-service-api`, base path `/vpe/api` (`application.yml` `spring.webflux.base-path`): `GET /visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn}`, `POST /user/add`, `PUT /user/update-password/{username}`, `PUT /user/change-status/{username}`, `DELETE /clear-cache/{msisdn}`, `GET /clear-all-cache` (`RouteConfiguration.kt`, lines 59/86/98/111/124/139 — re-verified this run, unchanged).
91	- **OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak** — `rsc-report-viewer` login, issuer `https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` (dev config; confirm prod issuer separately — not confirmed).
92	- **MariaDB** — shared L2 cache table + config/user data (`rsc_config_db`) for `rsc-service-api`; transaction/event/summary report tables (`rsc_reporting_db`) written by `rsc-data-loader` and read by `rsc-report-viewer`. Connection via `mariadb-java-client` + HikariCP.
93	- **SNMP traps** — `CommonSNMPManager` (internal `snmp-log-utils` lib) sends traps for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, and app start/stop, via a configured shell script (`service-api.snmp.snmp-file-path: /hms/scripts/sample_snmp.sh`).
94	- **Distributed tracing** — Brave/Zipkin via Micrometer Tracing (`micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave`), trace ID surfaced in logs and as `X-Trace-Id`-style context (`Context.traceId`).
95	- **Liquibase** — schema migration/versioning for all four MariaDB schemas (`liquibase.sh`, `data/*/changelog`, `docker/docker-compose-db-migrate-*.yml`).
96	
97	## Test Conventions
98	- **Framework**: JUnit 5 via `spring-boot-starter-test`, `mockk` (Kotlin-idiomatic mocking) and `mockito-kotlin` as mocking libraries, `reactor-test` for WebFlux/coroutine flows. Report viewer additionally uses `spring-security-test` and `kotlin-test`.
99	- **Layout**: mirrors main source package structure under `src/test/kotlin/...` (`rsc-service-api`) and `src/test/java/...` (`rsc-report-viewer`); one test class generally per main class (e.g. `DefaultSpmlConnectorAdapterTest.kt`, `VisitorAuthenticatorTest.kt`, `SecurityConfigurerTest.kt`, validator-specific tests under `validator/`).
100	- **Naming**: `<ClassUnderTest>Test.kt`/`.java`; some split across numbered files for large suites (`TpsLoggerImplTest`, `TpsLoggerImplTest1`, `2`, `3`).
101	- **Test config**: `rsc-service-api/src/test/resources/application.yml` overrides for test runs.
102	- **Local run**: `mvn clean install -DskipTest` for build; `docker-compose-dev-infa.yml` + `docker-compose-dev-test-infa.yml` for local infra, then `docker-compose-db-migrate-rsc-*-db.yml` / `*-test-db.yml` to create schemas (Readme.md). `data/initial-data/add-user.sql` seeds users; partitioning script must be run before load (`trx_events_log`, `trans_log`, `tps_log`).
103	- **External dependency simulation**: `simulators/rsc-service-simulator/` (WireMock) stands in for the SPML gateway with canned scenario mappings (roaming true/false, unauthorized, bad request, not-acceptable, internal error, delayed response) — useful for both manual and integration testing of `rsc-service-api` without a real HLR/VLR connection.
104	- **CI**: No CI pipeline definition (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, GitHub Actions) found in the repository — re-confirmed this run (no matches for `Jenkinsfile`/`*.gitlab-ci*`). Not confirmed how/where automated tests run in CI. SonarQube scan is documented as a manual `mvn sonar:sonar` command (Readme.md), not confirmed to be wired into CI.
105	
106	## Risk Notes
107	- **External SPML/HLR dependency is the critical path** — every roaming check calls out to the telecom Provisioning Gateway; `DefaultSpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps failures in generic `InternalErrorException`, and a documented open question in `docs/hld/hld_review.md` notes SPML connector delay/TPS is not fully understood ("What is the average delay for SPML connector at the moment", "Max tps for calling SPML is 50TPS... Need to monitor the SPML TPS"). Rate limiting is fixed at 50/s — worth confirming behavior under throttling/backpressure.
108	- **Hybrid cache correctness** — L1 (Caffeine, per-instance) vs L2 (MariaDB, shared) can diverge; sync runs every 30s, cleanup every 2min (`application.yml` `cache.sync.scheduler`, `cache.cleanup.scheduler`). The most recent product commit (`5c0d862`, tagged into release `2.0.5`, still HEAD's most recent product change as of this run) specifically touched `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt` to "fix non & neighbouring countries cache time based on Vlr" — this cache-TTL-by-VLR logic remains the freshest change and should stay a priority regression-test area until a newer commit supersedes it. Multi-instance deployments should also be tested for stale-cache/race conditions, especially around `clear-cache`/`clear-all-cache` admin endpoints only clearing local vs distributed state.
109	- **Auth is custom, not framework-based, in rsc-service-api** — `VisitorAuthenticator` manually decodes Basic-Auth header and checks a DB-backed user table with a custom `PasswordService`; no Spring Security filter chain enforcing this, so any new route must remember to call `authenticate(...)` explicitly or it is unprotected by default (`RouteConfiguration.kt`).
110	- **Two different auth models across modules** — `rsc-service-api` (Basic Auth + DB users) vs `rsc-report-viewer` (Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC) — a tester must treat these as separate boundaries with separate credentials.

# Project Context

Last updated: 2026-08-31 — refresh (run_id `2026-08-31`), output relocated to configured
`output_dir` = `/hms/projects/m1_rsc/rsc108/rsc-service-qa-pipeline` per explicit user
instruction for this run (no `config/pipeline.config.yaml` exists in the target project, so the
pipeline default would otherwise have been `./output` inside `rsc-service/`; a prior copy of
this file exists there and was used as the baseline for this refresh). Re-verified against the
current working tree (`git log -1` still `2828ad6` / tag `2.0.5`, `git status --short` shows only
the untracked QA-pipeline scaffold files — no product source changes, `git diff HEAD --stat`
empty). Spot-re-checked this run: `pom.xml` version/module list, `RouteConfiguration.kt` route
list, `application.yml` keys, absence of CI config, `super-csv` dependency in
`rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`, Keycloak `issuer-uri`, and presence of the checked-in `.p12`/`.jks`
keystores. All prior claims held; no corrections needed this cycle.

## Overview
`rsc-service` ("Roaming Status Check API for M1", version `2.0.5`, `pom.xml`) is a telecom backend built for M1 Singapore. It checks whether a given MSISDN (mobile subscriber number) is currently roaming by querying the operator's HLR/VLR data through an SPML provisioning-gateway connector, caches results, logs transactions/events, and exposes reporting on those transactions through a separate web UI. It is a Maven multi-module project with three deployable modules: a reactive API service, a log/report data loader, and a Thymeleaf/Keycloak-secured report viewer (`pom.xml` `<modules>`).

## Tech Stack
- **Language/runtime**: Kotlin 1.9.25 (main API + data loader), Java 21 (report viewer), JDK 21 target (`pom.xml` `java.version`).
- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.5.6 (parent POM), Spring WebFlux + Kotlin coroutines (`rsc-service-api`), Spring MVC + Thymeleaf (`rsc-report-viewer`), Spring Data JDBC/JPA.
- **Build**: Maven, multi-module reactor (`rsc-service-parent`).
- **Key libraries**: `kotlinx-coroutines-reactor`, `resilience4j` (rate limiter, time limiter) for SPML call protection, `caffeine` (in-memory L1 cache), `mariadb-java-client`, `micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave` + `zipkin-reporter-brave` for distributed tracing, `hms-common-util` / `snmp-log-utils` (internal hSenid libraries for SNMP alarms), `spml-gw` (internal SPML connector library used to talk to the telecom provisioning gateway), Gson, `super-csv` (report export, confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`), `mockk` / `mockito-kotlin` / `spring-boot-starter-test` / `reactor-test` for testing.
- **Data store**: MariaDB 11.4 (two logical DBs: `rsc_config_db` for users/config, `rsc_reporting_db`/`rsc-reporting` for transaction & event logs) — confirmed via `application.yml` datasource URLs and `data/config_db*`, `data/reporting_db*` Liquibase changelogs.
- **Auth**: `rsc-service-api` uses HTTP Basic-style `Authorization` header (base64 `user:password`) validated against a DB-backed user table (`VisitorAuthenticator.kt`). `rsc-report-viewer` uses OAuth2/OIDC login against Keycloak (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`, `issuer-uri: https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` — confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/resources/application.yml`).
- **Infra**: Docker Compose files for local dev DB/infra and Liquibase migrations (`docker/docker-compose-*.yml`, `liquibase.sh`), HAProxy 2.6.0 mentioned as the fronting LB (Readme.md software versions list), RedHat 9.4 target OS.

## Architecture
Monolith-ish multi-module system, not a single deployable — three independently built/deployed Spring Boot apps sharing the same MariaDB schemas and internal libraries:

```
Roaming client (e.g. VPE/other operator)
      │ HTTPS + Basic Auth  (GET /vpe/api/visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn})
      ▼
rsc-service-api (WebFlux, functional routers)
      │
      ├─ auth: VisitorAuthenticator ──► rsc_config_db (users/roles)
      ├─ workflow: WorkflowChain (chain-of-responsibility validators)
      │     NumberLengthValidator → NumberRangeValidator → CheckInCache →
      │     SpmlExistsValidator → SingleMsisdnRoamingValidator → MultiSimStatusValidator
      ├─ cache: DistributedMsisdnCacheManager — L1 Caffeine (per-instance) + L2 MariaDB
      │     (shared/distributed), background sync (30s) + cleanup (2min) schedulers
      ├─ connectors: SpmlConnectorAdapter → spml-gw library → SPML/XML provisioning
      │     gateway (HLR/VLR search + multi-SIM member check), rate-limited via resilience4j
      ├─ logs: TransLogger / EventLogger → transaction & event log tables/files
      └─ snmp: CommonSNMPManager → SNMP traps for DB errors, high TPS, timeouts, start/stop

rsc-data-loader (Kotlin, scheduled batch/log processor)
      reads trans/event log files → parses via ColumnSpec/Transformers →
      writes to rsc_reporting_db (trans_log, tps_log, trx_events_log tables) →
      ReportGeneratorService produces summary/detail report tables

rsc-report-viewer (Spring MVC + Thymeleaf, Keycloak OAuth2 login)
      ReportingController/ReportingService → DetailTransactionRepository (JPA/JDBC)
      → reads rsc_reporting_db → renders/downloads CSV reports (super-csv)
```

## Modules / Components
- **rsc-service-api** — Reactive API that answers roaming-status lookups for MSISDNs against the telecom HLR/VLR via SPML, with caching, validation chain, auth, and alarms. Path: `rsc-service-api/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/`
  - `api/` — WebFlux functional route definitions (`RouteConfiguration.kt`) for `visitorInfo`, user management (`/user/add`, `/user/update-password`, `/user/change-status`), and cache admin (`/clear-cache`, `/clear-all-cache`).
  - `workflow/` — `WorkflowChain`/`WorkFlowStep` chain-of-responsibility pattern driving the roaming-check pipeline and building the response/cache entry.
  - `validator/` — individual chain steps: MSISDN length/range checks, SPML existence check, single-MSISDN roaming determination, multi-SIM status check, cache short-circuit (`CheckInCache`).
  - `connectors/` — `SpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps the internal `spml-gw` library to send XML SPML requests (`search_request.xml`, `multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`) and parse HLR/VLR/call-barring (odboc) XPath responses.
  - `cache/` — `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager` (hybrid L1 Caffeine + L2 MariaDB cache), `CacheRepository`, sync/cleanup schedulers.
  - `auth/` — Basic-auth style `VisitorAuthenticator`, DB-backed user repo/entity, `PasswordService`, `UserRoles` (ADMIN/USER).
  - `logs/` — `TransLogger`/`EventLogger`/TPS logger writing transaction, event, and TPS logs consumed later by `rsc-data-loader`.
  - `snmp/`, `alarms/` — SNMP trap alarms for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, app start/stop.
  - `error/` — typed exceptions (`ApiErrorException`, `InternalErrorException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `DefaultErrorException`) mapped to HTTP statuses.
- **rsc-data-loader** — Batch/scheduled Kotlin service that parses trans/event/TPS log files and loads them into the reporting DB, then generates summary reports. Path: `rsc-data-loader/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/dataloader/`
  - `logspecs/` — column specs and field `Transformer`s (`NullColumnTransformer`, `BooleanFieldTransformer`, `FieldWithColumnNameTransformer`) describing log file layouts.
  - `service/lineProcessor/`, `service/loadInFileProcessor/` — log line/file ingestion pipeline (`TransLogProcessor`, `LoadInFileProcessor`).
  - `service/reportGenerator/` — `ReportGeneratorService`/`ReportGeneratorRepository` builds summary/detail report tables.
  - `service/lock/` — `DistributedTemplateLockManager` (DB-based distributed locking, likely to keep multi-instance loaders from double-processing).
  - `snmp/` — SNMP alarm config mirroring the API module.
- **rsc-report-viewer** — Spring MVC web app (Java) with Keycloak SSO login for viewing/exporting roaming transaction reports. Path: `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/java/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/viewer/`
  - `controller/` — `LoginController`, `ReportingController`.
  - `service/`, `service/impl/` — `ReportingService`/`ReportingServiceImpl`.
  - `repository/` — `DetailTransactionRepository`, `UserRepository` (JPA).
  - `configuration/` — `SecurityConfiguration`, `AuthoritiesConverter`, `CustomAuthenticationEvents` (Keycloak/OAuth2 role mapping).
  - `validator/` — `DetailTransactionReportValidator`, `DateFormatValidator` for report query params.
  - `health/` — `DbHealthChecker`.
  - `keycloak/theme/` — custom Keycloak login theme.
- **data/** — Liquibase changelogs for the four MariaDB schemas: `config_db`, `config_db_test`, `reporting_db`, `reporting_db_test`, plus `initial-data/` scripts (user seeding, `trx_events_log`/`trans_log`/`tps_log` partitioning). Path: `data/`
- **simulators/rsc-service-simulator/** — WireMock-based standalone simulator (jar + `mappings/`) used to fake SPML/downstream responses for testing (roaming true/false, unauthorized, bad-request, not-acceptable, internal-error scenarios). Path: `simulators/rsc-service-simulator/`
- **docs/** — HLD PlantUML/PNG diagrams (system context, API/report-viewer/data-loader component diagrams, deployment, DB designs) under `docs/hld/`, SRS/SOW/flow requirement docs under `docs/req/`, and real SPML XML/WSDL/XSD samples under `docs/spml_samples/`. Path: `docs/`
- **Documents/** — Untracked reference material (client-supplied SRS PDFs across versions `v0.0.2`–`v1.1.0`, SDP PDFs, SOW xlsx, flow/sequence diagrams, VPE OpenAPI spec, XSD/WSDL zips). Not code, useful background for requirements analysis. Path: `Documents/`
- **QA agent pipeline scaffold** (`config/`, `prompts/`, `templates/`, `output/`, `dashboard/`, `scripts/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`, root `README.md`) — this is tooling for the QA pipeline itself (this analysis run), not part of the deployed rsc-service product; confirmed untracked in `git status` in the target repo. Not a runtime component of the product under test.

## Integration Points
- **SPML (XML over HTTP, via internal `spml-gw` connector library)** — outbound integration to the telecom Provisioning Gateway for HLR/VLR search (`search_request.xml`) and multi-SIM member check (`multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`); WSDL/XSD in `rsc-service-api/src/main/resources/spml/wsdl/` and `docs/spml_samples/`. Rate-limited to 50 req/s via `resilience4j` (`application.yml` `resilience4j.ratelimiter.instances.spml-requests`).
- **REST (Basic Auth) inbound API** — `rsc-service-api`, base path `/vpe/api` (`application.yml` `spring.webflux.base-path`): `GET /visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn}`, `POST /user/add`, `PUT /user/update-password/{username}`, `PUT /user/change-status/{username}`, `DELETE /clear-cache/{msisdn}`, `GET /clear-all-cache` (`RouteConfiguration.kt`, lines 59/86/98/111/124/139 — re-verified this run, unchanged).
- **OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak** — `rsc-report-viewer` login, issuer `https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` (dev config; confirm prod issuer separately — not confirmed).
- **MariaDB** — shared L2 cache table + config/user data (`rsc_config_db`) for `rsc-service-api`; transaction/event/summary report tables (`rsc_reporting_db`) written by `rsc-data-loader` and read by `rsc-report-viewer`. Connection via `mariadb-java-client` + HikariCP.
- **SNMP traps** — `CommonSNMPManager` (internal `snmp-log-utils` lib) sends traps for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, and app start/stop, via a configured shell script (`service-api.snmp.snmp-file-path: /hms/scripts/sample_snmp.sh`).
- **Distributed tracing** — Brave/Zipkin via Micrometer Tracing (`micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave`), trace ID surfaced in logs and as `X-Trace-Id`-style context (`Context.traceId`).
- **Liquibase** — schema migration/versioning for all four MariaDB schemas (`liquibase.sh`, `data/*/changelog`, `docker/docker-compose-db-migrate-*.yml`).

## Test Conventions
- **Framework**: JUnit 5 via `spring-boot-starter-test`, `mockk` (Kotlin-idiomatic mocking) and `mockito-kotlin` as mocking libraries, `reactor-test` for WebFlux/coroutine flows. Report viewer additionally uses `spring-security-test` and `kotlin-test`.
- **Layout**: mirrors main source package structure under `src/test/kotlin/...` (`rsc-service-api`) and `src/test/java/...` (`rsc-report-viewer`); one test class generally per main class (e.g. `DefaultSpmlConnectorAdapterTest.kt`, `VisitorAuthenticatorTest.kt`, `SecurityConfigurerTest.kt`, validator-specific tests under `validator/`).
- **Naming**: `<ClassUnderTest>Test.kt`/`.java`; some split across numbered files for large suites (`TpsLoggerImplTest`, `TpsLoggerImplTest1`, `2`, `3`).
- **Test config**: `rsc-service-api/src/test/resources/application.yml` overrides for test runs.
- **Local run**: `mvn clean install -DskipTest` for build; `docker-compose-dev-infa.yml` + `docker-compose-dev-test-infa.yml` for local infra, then `docker-compose-db-migrate-rsc-*-db.yml` / `*-test-db.yml` to create schemas (Readme.md). `data/initial-data/add-user.sql` seeds users; partitioning script must be run before load (`trx_events_log`, `trans_log`, `tps_log`).
- **External dependency simulation**: `simulators/rsc-service-simulator/` (WireMock) stands in for the SPML gateway with canned scenario mappings (roaming true/false, unauthorized, bad request, not-acceptable, internal error, delayed response) — useful for both manual and integration testing of `rsc-service-api` without a real HLR/VLR connection.
- **CI**: No CI pipeline definition (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, GitHub Actions) found in the repository — re-confirmed this run (no matches for `Jenkinsfile`/`*.gitlab-ci*`). Not confirmed how/where automated tests run in CI. SonarQube scan is documented as a manual `mvn sonar:sonar` command (Readme.md), not confirmed to be wired into CI.

## Risk Notes
- **External SPML/HLR dependency is the critical path** — every roaming check calls out to the telecom Provisioning Gateway; `DefaultSpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps failures in generic `InternalErrorException`, and a documented open question in `docs/hld/hld_review.md` notes SPML connector delay/TPS is not fully understood ("What is the average delay for SPML connector at the moment", "Max tps for calling SPML is 50TPS... Need to monitor the SPML TPS"). Rate limiting is fixed at 50/s — worth confirming behavior under throttling/backpressure.
- **Hybrid cache correctness** — L1 (Caffeine, per-instance) vs L2 (MariaDB, shared) can diverge; sync runs every 30s, cleanup every 2min (`application.yml` `cache.sync.scheduler`, `cache.cleanup.scheduler`). The most recent product commit (`5c0d862`, tagged into release `2.0.5`, still HEAD's most recent product change as of this run) specifically touched `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt` to "fix non & neighbouring countries cache time based on Vlr" — this cache-TTL-by-VLR logic remains the freshest change and should stay a priority regression-test area until a newer commit supersedes it. Multi-instance deployments should also be tested for stale-cache/race conditions, especially around `clear-cache`/`clear-all-cache` admin endpoints only clearing local vs distributed state.
- **Auth is custom, not framework-based, in rsc-service-api** — `VisitorAuthenticator` manually decodes Basic-Auth header and checks a DB-backed user table with a custom `PasswordService`; no Spring Security filter chain enforcing this, so any new route must remember to call `authenticate(...)` explicitly or it is unprotected by default (`RouteConfiguration.kt`).
- **Two different auth models across modules** — `rsc-service-api` (Basic Auth + DB users) vs `rsc-report-viewer` (Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC) — a tester must treat these as separate boundaries with separate credentials.
- **MSISDN regex-driven business rules** are config-driven and easy to get subtly wrong: `service-api.roaming-inactive-msisdn`, `msisdn-validations.range`, `msisdn-status-cache.neighbouring-countries-vlrAddress` in `application.yml` directly control roaming/multi-sim/caching logic — any change to these regexes changes business behavior without a code change.
- **Log-to-report pipeline has multiple hops** (`rsc-service-api` writes trans/event logs → `rsc-data-loader` parses and loads into `rsc_reporting_db` → `rsc-report-viewer` reads/exports) — data can be lost or delayed at any hop; partitioning of `trx_events_log`/`trans_log`/`tps_log` must be pre-created or inserts fail (Readme.md warning).
- **Secrets/credentials in resources** — `rsc-service-api/src/main/resources/application.yml` contains a default DB password (`password`) and an SSL keystore password (`password`), and a committed `.p12` keystore and SPML client keystore (`spml/keystore/client.jks`) — confirmed still present, unchanged this run; confirm these are dev-only and rotated for other environments; not confirmed whether prod uses externalized secrets.
- **SNMP alerting depends on an external shell script path** (`/hms/scripts/sample_snmp.sh`) — if missing/misconfigured in an environment, DB error / high-TPS / timeout alarms silently won't fire.

## Not Confirmed
- Whether/where CI actually runs `mvn test`/`mvn verify` — no CI config file found in the repo (re-checked this run).
- Production Keycloak issuer/realm configuration (only a `localhost:8081` dev value was found).
- Exact list of consumers/clients calling `rsc-service-api` (referred to generically as "VPE"/other operator systems in code comments and docs) — not traced beyond the API contract itself.

# Changes — rsc-service (all tagged releases through 2.0.5 / 3.0.5)

Source: `git log`/`git show` on the `rsc-service` repository (all tags `0.0.1` → `2.0.5`,
`3.0.5`), cross-referenced with `output/context.md`.
Analyzed: 2026-08-31 (run_id `2026-08-31`)

## Scope note (read first)
This repo has two eras: an original build-out from **2022-06-24 to 2023-02-17** (tags `0.0.1`
through `1.0.8`, ~360 commits), then a **19-month gap**, then an active relaunch from
**2025-10-13 to 2026-01-20** (tags `2.0.0` through `2.0.5`/`3.0.5`, ~78 commits). Per the
request to cover all releases, both eras are included below. The 2022–2023 era is summarized
as consolidated, theme-level entries (dozens of individual commits grouped) since those
releases already shipped years ago and granular per-commit detail no longer serves current test
planning; the 2025–2026 era is itemized at commit level since it is the active release train.
Every entry still cites concrete commit hashes.

**Important history caveat**: tag `2.0.1` (2025-10-29, Hazelcast→Redis migration) is **not** an
ancestor of the current `HEAD`/`2.0.5`. The mainline that produced `2.0.2` onward branched from
`2.0.0` directly and re-did the Hazelcast removal a different way (MariaDB + Caffeine instead of
Redis). See **Unclear / Needs Clarification** — testers should not assume Redis is part of the
shipped system even though a `2.0.1` tag exists.

## Summary (change count by category)
- Breaking Changes: 9
- New Features: 8
- Enhancements: 9
- Bug Fixes: 8 (current era) + 1 consolidated legacy entry (dozens of commits)
- Refactors / Internal: 5
- Config / Infra: 10
- Unclear / Needs Clarification: 5

## Breaking Changes

- **JDK 17 → 21 upgrade, all three modules** — `rsc-service-parent`, `rsc-service-api`,
  `rsc-report-viewer`, `rsc-data-loader` all retargeted from JDK 17 to JDK 21, alongside Spring
  Boot 2.7.0 → 3.4.5 and Spring Cloud 2021.0.3 → 2024.0.0. Affected: whole project (build/runtime
  target). Ref: `5108ae2`, `18b9627`, `4fff795`, `09a5029` (release `2.0.0`)
- **Spring Boot further bumped 3.4.5 → 3.4.6 → 3.5.6; Spring Cloud → 2025.0.0** during the same

- **`rsc-report-viewer` login mechanism replaced with Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC** — adds

  `CacheRepositoryImpl`, `CacheCleanupScheduler`, `CacheSyncScheduler`). Ref: `d1b48dd`,
  `933f077` (release `2.0.2`)
- **Node ID removed from `rsc-data-loader` distributed-lock logs.** Ref: `796660b` (release
  `2.0.2`)
- **Unit test coverage added** for `rsc-service-api` (general) and for the concurrent
  cache-eviction fix specifically. Ref: `d73cbb2`, `8a011f1`, `5cc5536` (releases `2.0.2`,
  `2.0.3`)
- **spml-gw connector version corrections.** Ref: `6838fc2`, `a7b400d` (release `2.0.0`)
- **[Legacy] Numerous SNMP alarm-message/key refinements and connection-pool/TPS-throttling
  tuning** consolidated across `1.0.0`–`1.0.5`. Ref: `cbd9414`, `b68fa1b`, representative of
  ~15 similar commits in that window.

## Bug Fixes

- **Fixed: certificate files (`.p12`/`.jks`) getting corrupted during build** — the Maven
  resource-copy/token-filter step now excludes `*.p12`/`*.jks` instead of running the
  `VERSION`-token filter over them. Affected: `rsc-service-api` build/packaging. Ref: `4e9e96e`
  (release `2.0.0`)
- **Fixed: TPS report CSV not downloading** — corrected the download link path in the
  `tps-utilization.html` template from `/reporting/download/tps-utilization/...` to
  `/download/tps-utilization/...`. Affected: `rsc-report-viewer` reporting UI — worth confirming
  this path change is consistent with the actual `ReportingController` route mapping. Ref:
  `599ce75` (release `2.0.0`)
- **Fixed: transaction ID not appearing in logs** — root-caused to missing tracing
  configuration; fixed by adding `TracingConfiguration` to both `rsc-data-loader` and
  `rsc-service-api` and adjusting `logback.xml`. Applied twice (once per module, different
  dates). Affected: both modules' log correlation. Ref: `743d54e`, `4c76776`
- **Fixed: concurrent cache-eviction issue** in `CacheSyncScheduler`. Affected: `rsc-service-api`
  cache. Ref: `e55f7a0` (release `2.0.3`, mislabeled "rsc-report-api" — actual diff is in
  `rsc-service-api`)
- **Fixed: non/neighbouring-country cache expiry based on VLR** (see also Enhancements —
  this is a correctness fix to previously-added cache-TTL logic, not a new capability). Ref:
  `5c0d862` (release `3.0.5`)
- **Fixed: typo** in `rsc-report-viewer`'s `messages_en.properties`. Ref: `da989dc` (release
  `2.0.3`)
- **[Legacy, dozens of commits, `0.0.2`–`1.0.8`]** Consolidated bug-fix theme covering: SNMP
  trap message/key corrections; trans-log/trx-events-log field printing (auth status, terminated
  IP, request status) issues; MSISDN/roaming validation edge cases; detail-transaction report
  search/pagination/CSV-download issues; TPS/error-summary report calculation errors; data-loader
  multi-node log-processing and log-rotation issues; DB migration/Liquibase script errors;
  disabling summary CSV generation via new config; dangling distributed-lock cleanup on restart.
  Each was tracked against an internal bug ID in the commit message (Bug 46025 through Bug
  46560). Representative refs: `d66c0ad`, `7a5033c`, `f5ba113`, `4f6ac8b`, `08ed272`, `1785328`,
  `a924424`, `fa3a642`, `4b30272`, `874dada`, `abcc80e`, `56a6c99`, `136b50e`, `9b633a8`,
  `45a8f9c`, `3b862b2` (releases `0.0.2` through `1.0.8`)
- **[Legacy, 1.0.2] Report Viewer security hardening batch**: CSRF tokens added, Content-Security-
  Policy header set, X-Frame-Options set, SameSite + Secure cookie flags set, third-party JS
  comments removed, bootstrap dependency upgraded. Affected: `rsc-report-viewer`. Ref: `c6eba65`,
  `a1179b1`, `2c2eb24`, `50e48a5`, `b722ec3`, `700a12c`, `1e1a852`

## Refactors / Internal

- **`spring-cloud-starter-sleuth` replaced by Micrometer Tracing** in `rsc-data-loader` (part of
  the JDK21/Spring upgrade). Ref: `11ad80b` (release `2.0.0`)
- **Hazelcast config/properties stripped from `application.yml`** for both `rsc-service-api` and
  `rsc-data-loader` once the MariaDB/Caffeine cache landed. Ref: `e569ef5`, `54b64d6` (release
  `2.0.2`)
- **[Legacy] Report-viewer module bootstrapped from the internal "xcap" project reference
  code**, then progressively converted from Kotlin to Java and refactored (routing, model
  attributes, DB access). Ref: `1054b7d`, `ae27cd7`, `20c0271` (releases `0.0.1`–`0.0.2`)
- **[Legacy] Logback configuration consolidated/standardized** across all three modules. Ref:
  `bf907ec` (release `1.0.2`)
- **[Legacy] Report-generation and stored-procedure logic refactored** multiple times in
  `rsc-data-loader` during initial build-out. Ref: `fe39922`, `8e77dc5`, `84b6284`

## Config / Infra

- **Actuator exposure config** (see Breaking Changes) — `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include:
  "*"`, `base-path: /actuator`, `health.db`/`health.diskspace` enabled, `show-details: always`.
  Ref: `d89ae70`
- **New Liquibase changeset** `V1_4__rsc_cache_table.sql` added to `config_db` for the new L2
  cache table. Ref: `d1b1a33` (release `2.0.2`)
- **`oauth2-client` dependency added** to `rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`. Ref: `8085764` (release
  `2.0.0`)
- **`spring-cloud.version` bumped 2024.0.0 → 2025.0.0** (root and `rsc-data-loader` POMs). Ref:
  `fc81b34` (release `2.0.0`)
- **Redis introduced then not carried into the shipped mainline**: `redis` docker dev deployment
  added, Redis client/config wired into `rsc-service-api` (caching) and `rsc-data-loader`
  (distributed locks), Redis version bumped to 8.2 — all under tag `2.0.1`. None of this is
  present in the current `HEAD`/`2.0.5` tree (no `redis` references remain in source or `data/`).
  See Unclear section. Ref: `5ecb1b0`, `ab5990a`, `2ba4e00`, `3542f66`, `f1b8eac`, `e3e49b1`
- **[Legacy] Liquibase-based DB migration and install scripting introduced** for the initial
  schema rollout. Ref: `9b74cb1`, `afa3f4f`, `da20a1e` (releases `0.0.1`–`0.0.4`)
- **[Legacy] SonarQube scanning plugin added to the Maven build.** Ref: `19267fb` (release
  `0.0.2`)
- **[Legacy] SNMP alarm scenario config and connection-pool/TPS-throttling tuning.** Ref:
  `bcf207a`, `cbd9414`, `b68fa1b` (release `1.0.5`)

## Unclear / Needs Clarification

- **Tag `2.0.1` is not an ancestor of `HEAD`/`2.0.5`.** Its Redis-based Hazelcast replacement
  (`5ecb1b0`, `ab5990a`, etc.) exists only on that tag and on branch `origin/jdk-upgrade`; the
  `2.0.2`+ mainline branched from `2.0.0` and re-implemented the Hazelcast removal differently
  (MariaDB + Caffeine). It is not clear from the available history whether `2.0.1` was an actual
  shipped/rolled-back release (there is literally a commit `7184e7f`
  "`[maven-release-plugin] rollback the release of 2.0.1`" followed by a second `2.0.1` release
  commit `8bfb10f`) or an abandoned experiment. Recommend confirming with the release owner
  whether any environment is currently running the Redis-based `2.0.1` build before scoping
  Redis out of testing entirely.
- **Tags `3.0.5` and `2.0.5` are both dated 2026-01-20, with `2.0.5` as a child of `3.0.5` and no
  source changes between them** (only `[maven-release-plugin]` version-bump commits). It's
  unclear why the version number went `2.0.4` → `3.0.5` → back down to `2.0.5` with identical
  code. `context.md` (based on `pom.xml`) confirms `2.0.5` as the current version, so `3.0.5`
  appears to be a superseded/mistaken tag, but this isn't confirmed from commit messages alone.
- **Commit messages prefixed "`rsc-report-api |`"** (`e5e9fdb`, `5cc5536`, `e55f7a0`, `6a3d468`,
  `5c0d862`) actually all modify files under `rsc-service-api/`, not `rsc-report-viewer` or a
  `rsc-report-api` module (no such module exists in the repo). Treated as `rsc-service-api`
  changes throughout this document based on the diff contents, not the commit message text.
- **`45a8f9c` "Improved error handling and removed dangling distributed lock"** and **`3b862b2`
  "Fixed issue in handling partially completed logs when system restarts"** (release `1.0.6`)
  have no bug/ticket reference and no `component:` prefix, unlike most other commits in the repo.
  Diff shows both touch `rsc-data-loader` locking/log-processing code, but the specific trigger
  scenario isn't stated beyond the commit message.
- **`599ce75`'s route path change** (`/reporting/download/tps-utilization/...` →
  `/download/tps-utilization/...`) is described as a fix, but whether the corresponding
  `ReportingController` mapping was already at `/download/...` (making this purely a template
  fix) or whether other templates/links still reference the old `/reporting/download/...` path
  is not confirmed from this commit alone.
